units.text: We'll follow a tested revision across an environment boundary. Build once and deploy the identifiable artifact to development. If a check fails, stop. If it passes, keep the exact artifact for review rather than rebuilding it for production.

The promotion gate sends the same artifact to production, using separate permissions, configuration and secrets. A branch name isn't a security boundary. Keep the prior approved revision available and verify production after deployment.

Manual approval pauses the pipeline before the production action. The approver should know the proposed change and test evidence. Approve only the identified revision; rejection or expiry prevents promotion.

Provide the change summary, artifact identity, test results and recovery plan. Monitor executions that are waiting. Approval is a decision to proceed, not a second signature check or proof that production will remain healthy.

We'll verify the container that actually gets deployed. The build publishes an image identified by digest. Capture scan results for that digest and check your allowed severity and coverage before release.

A release policy can block a failed scan. Verify the required signature on the exact digest before deployment. Signing establishes provenance under your policy; it doesn't establish that the software has no vulnerabilities.

The pipeline stores the artifact under controlled encryption. A target action role can be assumed only by the intended pipeline principal. Its artifact and key access must be granted separately; trust alone doesn't let it read the artifact.

Follow the immutable artifact identifier into the target account. Verify the target role used and the deployment result before promoting to the next environment. If permissions fail, fix the specific missing trust, object or key access rather than broadening all three.

A cross-Region action still belongs to the pipeline in its home Region. CodePipeline copies the input artifact to the configured artifact store in the target action's Region. That store and its key are in the pipeline account.

Not every action type can run cross-Region. Keep incompatible actions in the appropriate Region and verify both artifact stores, keys and roles for a supported action. A copied artifact isn't proof that deployment completed.

We'll compare what each rollout exposes to the new release. A Lambda alias can split traffic between versions. A canary starts with a small share and shifts the rest after a successful observation period; a linear rollout shifts in regular increments.
Use configured checks and alarms to decide whether to continue. Rollback can move alias traffic back to the prior version. It doesn't undo external writes already made by the new version.

In the CodeDeploy-based E C S example, the new task set has its own target group. A configured test listener can validate the new tasks before production traffic moves. The existing task set continues serving during preparation.

Shift production traffic according to the selected configuration and inspect both application and load balancer health. Keep the prior task set for the configured window. This task-set workflow is specific to the deployment model shown.

All at once puts the new version in use most quickly, but exposes everyone together. Canary tests a small share. Linear advances in steps, while rolling changes batches of instances. Choose the curve the deployment target actually supports.

Blue green uses a replacement environment, which can make switching traffic back easier while the old one remains usable. Validate spare capacity and data compatibility before choosing it. Moving traffic back is not the same as undoing state changes.

We'll turn release risks into checks the team can verify. If a credential is exposed, treat it as compromised and follow authorized incident procedures to revoke or rotate it. Removing it from a commit does not make earlier copies harmless.

Notify the owner and review relevant activity without copying the secret into logs or tickets. Prefer scoped short-lived credentials, keep secrets out of source, and use preventive scans before merging.

CodeGuru Reviewer is legacy: existing repository associations can still work, but you can't make new ones. For new code-review work, evaluate an available option such as Amazon Q Developer. Profiling runtime performance answers a different question than reviewing source.
E C two Image Builder can create and test an image from a known base and components. Promote the exact tested image I D. A successful build without the required tests is not release approval.

Use the tested image in an approved launch template version and roll it out under health gates. Verify the replacement instances and application before continuing. Keep a known-good image and rollout plan for recovery.

The build tests and packages the SAM application. CloudFormation expands the transform and provisions the change, while CodeDeploy can shift traffic through the Lambda alias. One successful step doesn't prove the others worked.

Verify the deployed integration, then watch configured alarms while traffic shifts. If the release fails its health criteria, follow the approved rollback behavior. A successful transform is not evidence of a healthy production request.
